hypothesis: The staged FLA CUDA kernels may accelerate the existing Qwen attention path. Actual dispatch, compilation, and numerical parity must first be verified; speed is not measured here.
change: Only per-process optional-package dispatch changes through the pinned isolated overlay. Original full-vocabulary output projection, unmerged LoRA, prompts, cache, padding, batch size 16 and T=1 remain unchanged. Hub kernels are disabled; calls to the selected FLA implementation are counted. Restricted letter projection is not combined with this experiment.
validation: All 278 original teacher-validation states and 1390 decisions. No public test or authored confirmation labels participate in parity.
compute: Laptop only under run_heavy.py with four threads and unchanged thermal rules; worker deadline 12 minutes including compilation. No cloud spending or baseline environment changes.
promotion: Parity is necessary, not sufficient. Require separately measured improved latency under the original target-laptop temperature and contamination protocol. A warm/contaminated diagnostic cannot satisfy the speed gate. If parity fails, preserve the failure and do not relax thresholds. No runtime integration in this experiment.
implementation_evidence: Transformers 5.17.0 selects FLA through use_kernel_func_from_hub_with_fallback. Require a closure bound to fla.ops.gated_delta_rule and nonzero observed CUDA calls; reject silent fallback. Archive executed dependency sources and the pinned wheel/file hashes.
amendment: The first attempt is terminal with C-compiler discovery failure. Set child-only CC and CUDA_PATH to the existing pinned overlay toolchain because Triton default discovery uses sysconfig platlib. No numerical model change or threshold relaxation.
